text:
anya: FYI uploaded last night's regional cache heatmap + profiling run. big gaps and a weird insert hotspot in the kv store. attaching findings in-thread.
will: link? can you paste the top-line numbers here first?
maria: quick summary: overall global prefix cache_hit_rate = 61%, but distribution is: us-east 82%, eu-west 44%, ap-south 19%. miss rate spikes on small prefixes and user-scoped prefixes.
anya: exact metrics pulled from prometheus: `cache_hit_rate{region="us-east"}=0.82, cache_hit_rate{region="eu-west"}=0.44, cache_hit_rate{region="ap-south"}=0.19`. p50/hit latency is fine, but p99 on misses + fetch path jumps 220ms for eu and 380ms for ap.
jon: ouch. is this a routing problem (requests routed cold) or replication lag?
maria: combination. current keying uses `model:vX|prefix_hash|tenant_id` and replication is eventual via async replication daemon that piggybacks during normal writes. ap-south has very low warmup because we rarely route training/large traffic there.
will: any evidence of inconsistent keys or region-encoded keys?
anya: no region tag in key (we intentionally made keys region-agnostic). problem is consistent-hash shard placement + route policy: most ap-south requests are routed to ap-south serving nodes, which start cold. since replication is async and piggybacked on writes, ap-south rarely receives the writes. so misses.
perf-bot: profile summary: top CPU by symbol during cache insert path: zstd::decompress (34%), kv_shard_mutex_lock (18%), memcpy (12%). memory: frequent small allocations at ~64-256 bytes during metadata encode.
maria: profiling also showed a hot mutex in `kv_shard::insert_if_absent` — contention increases nonlinearly when prefetch bursts happen.
jon: any bandwidth/egress costs observed when we replicate aggressively? we need to balance egress vs latency.
anya: yes — naive full replication would increase cross-region egress ~3.2TB/day at current QPS. costly.
will: what are proposed mitigations?
anya: list so far: 1) bloom-filter per region to avoid blind misses (cheap negative check) 2) probabilistic replication: replicate top-K prefixes per tenant by access frequency; use a sliding-window sketch to pick K 3) on-route opportunistic prefetch: when routing to a cold region, fetch hot prefixes from a warm region on the first N requests and cache them async 4) change key hashing to include an affinity tag for long-lived prefixes so they map to same shard across regions 5) reduce zstd compression levels on hot-path inserts to cut CPU/decompress time 6) implement lock striping or switch to sharded RW lock to reduce insert contention 7) implement stale-while-revalidate TTL for prefix entries to return slightly older content while we warm.
maria: +1 for bloom filters and probabilistic replication. Also, we should avoid replicating large KV blobs — only replicate small, frequently-requested prefix stubs (pointer + small text) and lazily fetch the full payload.
jon: how about routing policy experiments? maybe route a small percentage (1-5%) of requests for a prefix to a warm region to seed local caches, instead of always local routing. would that create odd consistency?
anya: we can do a canary: 'seed-and-serve' policy where 2% of requests for a prefix from a cold region are proxied to a warm region, and we write the returned prefix into local cache with a short TTL. that should dramatically increase hit rate at low cost.
will: need to capture metrics: per-prefix miss->seed conversion rate, cross-region egress delta, p99 latency change. we should run it against top 500 prefixes first.
perf-bot: suggested experiment metrics: `prefix_miss_count`, `prefix_seed_count`, `cross_region_egress_bytes`, `cache_insert_latency_ms`, `kv_insert_cpu_seconds`, `mutex_wait_seconds` — sample at 10s resolution.
maria: also found a regression in last week's runtime rollout: kernel selector change increased CPU utilization on unpack/decode path causing slower inserts. that pushed insert latency from 12ms -> 28ms under load, amplifying the hotspot.
anya: rollback of that selector patch on test pool improved insert latency back to 13ms. we need to retest selection heuristics with the cache insert profile in mind.
jon: ok action items: - anya: run bloom-filter PoC in staging for eu-west + ap-south (due EOD Wed) - will: add seeds routing AB test config for top-500 prefixes (due next Tues) - maria: change zstd settings in a canary cluster and measure CPU insert cost (due Fri) - jon: cost estimate for probabilistic replication and stubbing approach (due Mon)
anya: logs/commands used for profiling if useful: ```curl -s "$PROM/api/v1/query?query=cache_hit_rate%7Bregion%3D%22ap-south%22%7D" | jq .``` ```perf record -F 99 -g -- ./kv_bench_insert; perf report```
will: any concerns about correctness or consistency with seeding? replica stubs need to be versioned, otherwise clients might see stale structured outputs.
maria: we will attach `schema_version` and `source_region` metadata to stubs; seeding will use short TTL and write a revalidation job if schema mismatch detected.
anya: good. I'll push a short RFC with the bloom filter design + seeding experiment config. posting the heatmap images in #eng-runtime artifacts channel. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
deploy-bot: canary build 2026.03.17-heatmap-seed created (sha: abf12c).
jon: thanks all. let's keep the experiments tight and measure cost tradeoffs before a full replication change. :thumbsup:
